name: Computers
description: Computers from Babbage to today: the five generations of machines, the operating systems and programming languages that run them, and artificial intelligence.

checkpoints.name: Before electronics
checkpoints.note: Babbage designs mechanical computers and Ada Lovelace writes the first program for one. Punched cards tabulate the census, and Turing describes a universal machine.

checkpoints.name: First generation: vacuum tubes
checkpoints.note: Wartime code-breaking and ballistics build Colossus and ENIAC. Machines that store their own programs follow, programmed in machine code and assembly, and Turing asks whether machines can think.

checkpoints.name: Second generation: transistors
checkpoints.note: Transistors make computers smaller and reliable. FORTRAN, LISP and COBOL become the first high-level languages, and the field of artificial intelligence is named.

checkpoints.name: Third generation: integrated circuits
checkpoints.note: Integrated circuits put many transistors on one chip. IBM's System/360 and minicomputers spread, BASIC opens programming to students, and Unix is born.

checkpoints.name: Fourth generation: microprocessors
checkpoints.note: The microprocessor puts a whole computer on a chip. C, the PC, DOS, the Mac and Windows follow, then Linux, Java and Python. AI goes through booms and winters, and Deep Blue beats Kasparov.

checkpoints.name: Fifth generation: AI and parallel machines
checkpoints.note: Graphics chips power deep learning, AlphaGo beats the best human at Go and ChatGPT brings AI to everyone. Phones run Android and iOS, and new languages such as Rust and Swift arrive.
